replace: return Object.freeze({ kind: 'versus' as const, rules });
why: The pre-fix exported boundary. VersusRules is a plain interface and versusDescriptor is exported, so a caller can hand-build a structurally valid MUTABLE rules object, pass it in, and then keep editing it -- silently rewriting the retained intent of a session already in progress. Freezing only the wrapper does not close that; snapshotting the fields does. Note the mutation still freezes the DESCRIPTOR, so a test asserting only Object.isFrozen(d) cannot kill it: the killing assertion is the post-hoc mutation of the caller's own object. Scoped to app-state.test.ts. expectFailures is the count MEASURED by this harness against the scoped `tests` on this branch, not a repo-wide count.
killedBy: SessionDescriptor construction versus rules -- retained intent is an immutable snapshot SNAPSHOTS an unvalidated mutable rules object -- the caller cannot alter it afterwards
